page: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, along with 260 MB of L3 cache. There are no onboard GPUs or local storage devices bundled, meaning persistent or temporary storage relies entirely on external remote storage attachments.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive single-threaded throughput alongside lower relative multi-core and I/O density. The instance achieves average ratings in single-core stress testing (1916.18) and PassMark overall CPU execution (7245.74), supported by instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. Multi-threaded stress testing (3927.87) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (25.75 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the constraints of its two physical cores. Similarly, uncached large-block memory bandwidth reaches 31.34 GB/sec for reads and 23.07 GB/sec for writes, which positions it in the lower tiers of memory bus throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff is a high memory-to-vCPU ratio against modest compute parallelism and zero local disk capacity. The configuration suits in-memory caching layers, medium relational databases, static web serving (measured at 7.48 GB/sec), and small-model inference tasks that demand substantial RAM capacity without intensive multi-core parallel calculation.

Benchmark results show average single-thread CPU performance (1916.18 in stress-ng) alongside moderate static web serving throughput of 7.48 GB/sec. However, raw multi-core scaling and memory throughput measure in the lower performance brackets due to the limited two-core physical footprint. This configuration suits memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as mid-sized relational databases, in-memory caching services, and low-parallelism enterprise background workers requiring generous memory headroom.
